title: Ines and the Typewriter
premise: In a print shop in a city on the brink of revolution, Odile Galloway, daughter of a typeface cutter, has learned that safety lies in anonymity. When a sealed letter arrives naming her family as holders of a document implicating a powerful general in a massacre, Odile must choose between burning the evidence and honoring a promise her late father made to a printer now branded an enemy of the state. As the city descends into violence, she smuggles the letter through checkpoints with help from a disillusioned soldier, discovering that memory itself can be an act of treason. In the end, Odile delivers the testimony to a tribunal of printers who set it in type and scatter a thousand copies through the streets—justice rendered not by courts, but by ink—though it costs her the shop, her brother's loyalty, and the quiet life she believed she was owed.
about_author: Mirabel Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archival restorer who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in municipal record offices. She writes historical fiction about the people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the print shop's final quiet weeks, Odile sorts type while her father cuts matrices and her brother Théo runs pamphlets for whichever faction pays. A dying courier leaves a sealed letter addressed to her father with instructions: deliver it to Aldous Renard, the printer who taught them all their trade, now declared an enemy. Odile wants to burn it; her father, before his sudden death days later, makes her promise. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Unable to resist, Odile breaks the seal and reads the testimony: her father witnessed the general's massacre of striking typesetters years ago and kept silent in exchange for the shop's survival. The letter is his confession and his penance. Théo, terrified, urges burning it and reports a stranger asking questions at the shop. Odile realizes the family was never invisible—only spared. Emotional beat: the collapse of the lie that neutrality protects anyone.

chapters.title: Crossing the Barricades
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with an interlude from the disillusioned soldier Camille Vasseur. The revolution erupts; checkpoints seal the districts. Odile and Camille, who once served the general and deserted after reading his orders, smuggle the letter toward Renard's hiding place. Théo betrays their route to the general's men to save the shop, forcing a chase across the burning quarter. Camille is captured covering her escape. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Set in Type
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile finds Renard dying in a cellar press, and rather than a single sealed letter, he asks for something louder: set the testimony in type and let the city read it. With the apprentice printers she sets the pages overnight; at dawn a thousand copies flood the streets, and the general's name becomes a verdict no court can revoke. Théo, reading a copy in the crowd, cannot meet her eyes. The shop burns; the truth does not. Emotional beat: grief transformed into permanence.
